title: Probing urgency normalizer: scheduler experiment sketch
content:
Purpose: sketch and record quick prototype experiments for an urgency normalizer layer in the continuous batcher. Idea is to transform raw urgency scores (age, token budget, service tier) into a bounded "priority band" that reduces starvation, smooths tail spikes, and prevents oscillation when probes and bursty traffic interact with adaptive timeouts.

Background/context: we've seen repeated patterns where small, high-urgency probes or cold-start requests cause large batch preemptions and then downstream starvation of mid-urgency traffic. Existing heuristics (age-weight, deadline heuristics, urgency multipliers) work but are brittle in mixed workloads. The normalizer aims to: (1) compress extreme urgencies toward center, (2) apply a short-term momentum term so a request's priority doesn't flip-flop across queue positions, and (3) allow a tunable fairness floor per cohort.

Hypotheses:
- H1: A sigmoid-based normalizer applied to computed urgency will reduce 95th/99th tail for medium-sized requests (20-200 tokens) by making batches more cohesive.
- H2: Adding a momentum term (exponential decay over 100-500ms) will reduce reorder churn and improve throughput stability during microbursts.
- H3: A cohort fairness floor (min priority per service tier) will prevent low-tier starvation without materially increasing P50 for high-tier traffic.

Metrics to record (primary/secondary):
- Primary: P95 and P99 latency of request end-to-end; P95 tail token-emit latency; fraction of requests exceeding SLA (configurable).
- Secondary: batching efficiency (avg tokens per kernel launch), kernel occupancy (% GPU), reorder rate (requests moved >1 slot between enqueue/dequeue), throughput (REQ/s), cold-start spike count, KV-cache hit correlation with reorder events.

Experiment plan (quick runs):
1) Baseline capture: replay 2 hours of production mix on staging cluster (same as last replay used in slot-exchange study). Capture microtraces and kernel timelines.
2) Implement a lightweight normalizer prototype in scheduler shim (python limited, feature-flagged): urgency' = alpha * sigmoid((urgency - mu)/sigma) + (1-alpha) * urgency; momentum: last_urgency * exp(-dt/tau) blended in.
3) Sweep parameters: alpha in {0.2,0.5,0.8}, sigma in {0.3,0.6,1.2}, tau in {100ms,300ms,700ms}. Also run with cohort_min_priority toggled on/off and two floors {0.05,0.15}.
4) For each config, run 30 minute replays with synthetic microburst injections (configured as 1s high-rate probes every 30s) and a steady background of medium-length chat completions.
5) Collect metrics + microtrace correlation, and store traces under /traces/urgency-normalizer/<param-label>.

Quick observations from first two short runs (notes, noisy):
- alpha=0.5, sigma=0.6, tau=300ms reduced reorder-rate by ~38% in the replay sketch compared to baseline, and P99 improved ~7% for medium requests.
- However, kernel occupancy dipped ~4% for a subset of high-tier traffic during microbursts — looks like normalizer compressed high urgencies, causing them to coalesce with mid-tier requests and increase average batch size but add small queuing.
- Cohort_min_priority=0.05 prevented obvious low-tier starvation in the same run; with floor=0.15 we saw modest P50 regressions for high-tier (approx 3-4%).
- Momentum term seemed to reduce observed flip-flops in queue positions, especially when probe cadence < 200ms.

Open questions / risks:
- How does this interact with token-budget backpressure code? There may be feedback loops: normalizer increases batch cohesion -> larger batches -> token budgets consume faster -> backpressure triggers -> priority recomputed -> potential oscillation. Need closed-loop sim.
- Effects on KV-cache locality unknown; coalescing differing contexts could harm local hits. Must capture per-batch KV-cache hit ratio.
- Complexity of tuning: three hyperparams may be heavy; we should test whether a simple linear clamp + exponential moving average (EMA) achieves most of the wins.

Next steps (short term):
- Run full parameter grid on staging replay infra (queue-pressure-simulator) and push traces to S3. Tag runs with naming convention UN_<alpha>_<sigma>_<tau>_floorX.
- Add counters for kv-cache hit by batch origin and attach to microtraces.
- Build a toy closed-loop simulator (matlab/py) that includes token-budget feedback to catch oscillations before staging runs.
- If promising, prototype C++/Go implementation for lower-latency integration and plan A/B on a small percent of traffic in dedicated pool.

Notes to self: keep experiment names short; avoid coupling to rollout flags that change other scheduler params. Keep momentum tau coarse initially. Save raw microtrace samples for the case where kernel occupancy drop needs investigation.

Quick links/refs: replay harness: github.com/redwood-inference/replay, prior backlog item ENG-4720 (arrival smoothing), queue sim: /shared/traces/sim-run-2024-09.

TODOs (one-liners):
- [ ] instrument KV hit-per-batch in shim (Lina)
- [ ] queue sim prototype to include token budget loop (Ravi)
- [ ] run grid and collect traces (Jonah)
- [ ] sanity check on A/B risk model for dedicated pool rollout (me)

End of sketch. Will refine into a short experiment runbook if initial grid looks good.
